text:
acme_corp: hey, we started seeing a big uptick in 429s and tail latency from our dedicated pool around 09:12 UTC. Our app uses lots of long-context calls (~60k tokens). Are you seeing anything on your side?

erin_support: sorry to hear that — can you paste a sample request id or correlation id? also which dedicated tenant id?

acme_corp: tenant=acme-prod-42, sample rid=rid-0a1b2c3d. Errors look like "quota_exceeded: request throttled" but the billing/usage dashboard shows no quota breach. Latency spikes to 2s+ for generation start.

deploy-bot: [autoscale] pool=d-42 action=scale_down->scale_up reason=cpu_burst window=60s event_id=evt-7753

tom_infra: thanks @acme_corp and @erin_support — pulling infra traces. Quick hypothesis: KV cache pressure from long contexts causing repeated eviction/regen and backpressure on the request queue -> short throttles. Need KV metrics.

nora_sre: can you run this in your tenant console and share results?

```
# check kv cache hit/evict
redwoodctl metrics query --tenant acme-prod-42 --metric kv_cache_evictions --range 15m
redwoodctl metrics query --tenant acme-prod-42 --metric kv_cache_hit_rate --range 15m
```

ryan_ml: also helpful: sample model, seq_len, and whether you're pinning a specific variant or using routing fallback. Long contexts + mixed seq lengths are the worst for fragmentation.

acme_corp: model=gpt-neox-20b, variant=quant-fp8, seq=60k, pin=true. Running the metrics now, will paste.

acme_corp: paste metrics: 

```
kv_cache_evictions: spikes at 09:08->09:14 with ~4.2k evictions/min
kv_cache_hit_rate: dropped to 12% at spike (normally ~78%)
queue_wait_time_p95: increased from 30ms -> 1.6s
```

erin_support: that matches the theory — when hit rate collapses we see regen cost per request (warm-up) and the serving runtime slows, autoscaler sees short-lived cpu/mem drops and sometimes scales down too aggressively, then scale-up is delayed causing transient throttles (429).

tom_infra: two actionable items: 1) prevent scale-down during sustained high eviction windows (set autoscale_cooldown to 10m for this pool), 2) enable larger per-tenant KV capacity or eviction_threshold tuning for long-context workloads. I can push a temporary override.

acme_corp: please do. Also our app can't tolerate 1.6s spikes. Is there a recommended config for long contexts?

nora_sre: recommended short-term config:
- autoscale.cooldown_seconds: 600
- kv.cache.reserve_percent: 25
- concurrency.limit_per_worker: reduce to 8 (to reduce memory churn)

ryan_ml: for longer-term: consider splitting very long sessions into progressive summaries or using client-side prefix caching to avoid full KV regen on every request. Also try pinned cold-start warmup: schedule a low-rate keepalive to keep KV entries resident.

tom_infra: pushing override now -> hold.

deploy-bot: [override] pool=d-42 autoscale.cooldown_seconds=600 kv.cache.reserve_percent=25 set_by=tom_infra event=evt-7754

acme_corp: saw immediate improvement in p95 within ~2m, 429s dropped to normal. Thanks. Curious — any signal we should monitor to know this is starting again?

nora_sre: monitor kv_cache_hit_rate (alert if <30% for >2m), kv_cache_evictions (>500/min sustained), and queue_wait_time_p95 (>500ms). We'll also add a temporary dashboard for your tenant.

erin_support: logging next steps in the ticket and escalating to eng runtime to add a policy: automatic cooldown extension when eviction rate > threshold. @tom_infra @nora_sre assigning to runtime oncall.

ryan_ml: adding repro note: if you can share a scrubbed request pattern that hits 60k tokens repeatedly, we can run a local sim and propose better eviction heuristics.

acme_corp: will produce a scrubbed trace and upload to the ticket. thanks all :heart: :thumbsup:

nora_sre: marking this thread for follow-up — creating internal task to investigate cache fragmentation and autoscale interplay. ETA preliminary findings 48h.

erin_support: resolving transient throttles for now, keeping ticket open until runtime task closes. If anything regress ping this thread or DM. :wave:
